concepts.why: Non-caseating microgranulomas, elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme level, and erythematous mucosa in the colon and rectum are characteristic of sarcoidosis.
Chronic abdominal pain, diarrhea, and non-caseating microgranulomas are consistent with Crohn's disease, although the absence of rectal bleeding and weight loss is less typical.
Chronic diarrhea and erythematous mucosa in the colon are consistent with ulcerative colitis, but the presence of non-caseating microgranulomas and involvement of the terminal ileum are less typical.
Chronic diarrhea and non-caseating microgranulomas could be seen in gastrointestinal amyloidosis, although this diagnosis would require further confirmation with biopsy and staining.
Chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, and non-caseating microgranulomas could be seen in Whipple's disease, although the negative Tropheryma whipplei testing makes this diagnosis less likely.

Chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, and non-caseating microgranulomas could be seen in common variable immunodeficiency, although this diagnosis would require further confirmation with immunoglobulin level testing.

Chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, and non-caseating microgranulomas could be seen in autoimmune enteropathy, although this diagnosis would require further confirmation with serologic testing and response to immunosuppressive therapy.

Chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, and erythematous mucosa in the colon and rectum could be seen in eosinophilic gastroenteritis, although the absence of eosinophilia on biopsy makes this diagnosis less likely.

Chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, and non-caseating microgranulomas could be seen in graft-versus-host disease, although this diagnosis would require a history of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

Hereditary hemochromatosis and hepatosplenomegaly could be seen in primary biliary cholangitis, although this diagnosis would require further confirmation with liver function testing and serologic testing.

rationales.F09: Non-caseating microgranulomas are highly suggestive of sarcoidosis.
rationales.F11: Elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme level is a strong indicator of sarcoidosis.
